findings.title: A malformed or oversized inbound update raises KeyError/NoMethodError/ValidationError out of poll and aborts the whole gateway process
findings.recommendation: In Transport#poll, route a per-update normalization failure through the unsupported_envelope seam the normalizer already has (normalizer.rb:107-113) instead of letting it raise, so one bad update costs one digest-bound disposition rather than the gateway; keep the ValidationError on the envelope constructor as the last-resort guard.

findings.title: A 409 from sendMessage/editMessageText raises PollerConflictError, which DeliveryDrainer cannot read, so the drainer thread dies with the row stranded claimed
findings.recommendation: Make the Net::HTTPConflict branch method-aware in Client#call: a 409 on an idempotent read stays PollerConflictError, a 409 on a send takes the transport_failure(idempotent, ...) mapping the else branch at client.rb:82-84 already applies. No new class, no new branch shape.

findings.title: Throttling signalled as ok:false error_code:429 inside an HTTP 200 body loses the authoritative retry_after and becomes an ambiguous send instead of a deferral
findings.recommendation: Extend the ok:false branch to route error_code == 429 through the same Comms::ThrottledError.new('rate limited', retry_after: retry_after_from(body)) construction client.rb:72 already uses. If the coordinator can establish Telegram never answers 200-with-ok:false-429, close this instead of fixing it.

findings.title: The bot token is reachable through Client#inspect, and the effective transport timeouts are not observable
findings.recommendation: Drop :token from the attr_reader at client.rb:27 (nothing outside the class uses it; path_for reads @token directly) and add :open_timeout/:read_timeout so comms doctor can report the effective bound.

findings.title: comms doctor's TLS check asserts the origin string, not the effective verification mode
findings.recommendation: Have tls_ok? compare the client's effective verify_mode rather than the origin string; the reader addition F14-OBS-01 already asks for supplies it. Do not add an https:// host allowlist - expected_bot_id already pins the authenticated surface identity. Note the committed behavior is verified safe; this is a latent control gap.

findings.title: client.rb's header calls a timed-out send 'genuinely irreconcilable', contradicting the repository's own rule that ambiguous sends remain durable unknown
findings.recommendation: Replace the parenthetical at client.rb:13-14 with the durable layer's own word: the send's outcome is unknown and stays unknown until the operator resolves it. Comment-only; optionally align the three echoes (transport.rb:10-11, README line 9, test header).

findings.title: Client#read_timeout is injectable but no surface descriptor can set it, so poll_timeout_s above the built-in 65s read timeout is unreachable
findings.recommendation: None - the simple path already delivers the property (max_response_bytes is reachable, defaults are bounded, CLAIM_TTL_S bounds the stall). Add the descriptor key only if an operator later needs a poll longer than 65s.

blind_spots: Whether Telegram answers 200-with-ok:false-429 for sendMessage is unverified (F14-RES-01 stays medium/minor). No live API call was made.
Whether Telegram can return 409 on a send is unverified; the code behavior is proven by probe, the trigger is not (F14-COR-01).
Whether a real update can carry a message with no 'from' (channel posts) is unverified; no Bot API spec was read in this checkout (F14-REL-01).

Six comms test files were not run (callback_ack_crash, comms_cli_ops, comms_adr049_consistency, comms_evidence_gated_approval, canonical_cross_surface_composition, experience_harness) - a duplicate of either major finding would surface there rather than here.

gateway_admission.rb was read only at 85-130, gateway.rb only at 50-60 and 150-309, and binding.rb / admission.rb / approval_prompt.rb / rendering.rb were not read at all, so F14-REL-01's downstream admission consequence is characterized from partial context.

No load or soak evidence exists for this adapter; the fixture supports duplicate/reorder/lose but no test in either telegram file exercises them, so the scalability lens is reviewed from constants and guards rather than from evidence.
